# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🤙]

## Thinking

Topology check first, before I send anything:

- I am Deaf: I hear nothing. My **speech** reaches both Mute and Blind; my **gestures** reach only Mute.
- Mute cannot speak. Mute hears my speech and sees my gestures, but the only way Mute can ever reach **me** is by gesturing.
- Blind hears and speaks. Blind's words reach only Mute (I can't hear them). Blind's only way to reach **me** is gestures — which is exactly what Blind just did: 🖐 🤙.

So the lifelines are: my speech carries the bomb's visuals to both; Mute speaks the manual to Blind, who acts; and anything that must reach me comes back as signs. Blind's 🖐 🤙 looks like the natural finger-count code — open hand = 5, shaka = 6 — but it could also be "hello / answer me". Either way it proves Blind wants a channel to me, so I should fix a sign vocabulary in words now, while everyone can hear the agreement, since Blind can't see any code demonstration and Mute can't speak one. Then I ask Mute to confirm the channel with a thumbs-up, ask Blind to explain the 5-6 to Mute in words, and hand Mute the full readout for the manual.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Bomb readout, everything I can see: display shows 1. Light is green. Seven wires, left to right: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue.")
speak(text="I am Deaf: I will never hear a word either of you says. My only ear is my eyes for hand signs. So Mute can only ever talk to me in gestures, and Blind can only reach me through gestures too. I can hear nobody, but I can feed you both everything I see in words like this.")
speak(text="Proposed sign code for signing TO me, one sign at a time: thumbs up means yes or confirmed, thumbs down means no, raised palm means stop or wait, waving hand means hello. Digits by extended fingers: fist is 0, index is 1, two fingers is 2, three fingers is 3, four fingers is 4, open hand is 5, shaka is 6. For 7 to 9, send shaka plus the remainder: shaka then index is 7, shaka then two fingers is 8, shaka then three fingers is 9.")
speak(text="Blind: I saw your two signs, open hand then shaka. Under the code above that reads 5 then 6, but I cannot know what you meant. Please tell Mute in words what those signs meant, and tell Mute everything you feel on the bomb: batteries, ports, labels, serial, anything under your hands.")
speak(text="Mute: look up the manual for a display of 1, a green light, and seven wires in the order red, white, yellow, orange, green, purple, blue. Speak the cutting instructions aloud for Blind to carry out, and sign me anything I need to know using the digit code. Confirm you heard me by signing thumbs up to me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

## Thinking

Both confirmations arrived: Mute sent 👍 🖐, Blind sent 👍 ✋. Under my round-1 code those read "yes" plus either "5" (open hand) or "stop/wait" (raised hand) — I created a collision between 🖐 and ✋, so I can't trust either reading. Mute must resend under a tightened code.

Bigger structural discovery I have to fix: **Mute cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures.** There is no direct Mute→Blind channel at all. The manual knowledge can only reach the operator's hands through me: Mute gestures the manual answer to me (I see it), and I speak it aloud (Blind hears it). I am the relay, whether I like it or not — so the gestural vocabulary has to be rich enough to carry an actual cutting instruction: a marker, a "cut" verb, digits, and a done signal. Blind's 👍 ✋ I read as "confirmed, holding" — which is exactly right, because nobody has valid instructions yet. Nobody touches anything this round.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Both of you confirmed. Nobody cuts anything yet. Important change to the plan: Mute cannot speak at all, and Blind cannot see signs, so Mute can never reach Blind directly. I am now the relay. Mute reads the manual and gestures the instruction to me. I say it out loud. Blind carries it out.")
speak(text="Final sign code, no overlaps. Thumbs up: yes, correct. Thumbs down: no, cannot find it. Raised hand: stop, wait, hold. Waving hand: repeat, I do not understand. OK sign: a manual instruction follows. Clapping hands: cut wire, the next signs give the position. Both hands raised: module solved, all done. Pointing at you: Mute, I need something from you.")
speak(text="Digits, one sign each: fist is 0, index up is 1, victory is 2, love-you hand is 3, vulcan salute is 4, open hand is 5, shaka is 6, horns is 7, crossed fingers is 8, pinched fingers is 9. Digits in a row form one number and end at the first non-digit sign. For two cuts, send clap plus digit, then clap plus digit again, in cutting order.")
speak(text="Fresh full readout for the manual lookup: the display shows the number 1. The light is green. Seven wires, positions 1 to 7 left to right: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue. That is everything visible: no other markings, labels or readings.")
speak(text="Mute: your last signs were thumbs up then open hand. Under the new code open hand means 5. If that meant cut wire 5, resend it cleanly as OK sign, then clapping hands, then open hand. If it meant something else, resend it in the new code. Then find the rule for this module. If you need the visuals repeated, sign pointing at you. If the module is not in the manual, sign thumbs down.")
speak(text="Blind: hands completely still until you hear me say the words cut wire followed by a number. Right now, describe aloud for Mute everything under your hands: battery count, indicators, plates, ports, the serial number letter by letter and digit by digit, and how each of the seven wire positions feels. Mute hears you even though you cannot see each other. When you hear me say cut wire and a number, cut the wire at that position.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👏 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

## Thinking

Mute's message decodes cleanly under our code: 👌 (instruction follows) 👏 (cut wire) 🖐 (digit 5) — **cut wire 5**, which on my readout is the green wire. That was sent deliberately after I asked for an unambiguous resend, and the completion signal is absent, so I relay it now and make Blind report the result aloud for Mute to verify. Blind's 👍 ✋ confirms Blind is holding and ready. One cut, position five, nothing else until the next signal.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Relaying Mute's instruction now. Blind: cut wire 5. That is position 5 counting from the left, the wire I see as green. Cut only that one wire. Touch nothing else.")
speak(text="Blind, after you cut: take your hands off the bomb and speak aloud everything that changes: the light, any display, any sound. Mute hears you and will check it against the manual.")
speak(text="Mute: instruction received as cut wire 5 and relayed. When Blind cuts, listen to the report. If the module is solved, sign me both hands raised. If more cuts are needed, sign clap plus the next digit. If that was wrong or dangerous, sign raised hand and I will shout for Blind to stop. If there was no such rule, sign thumbs down.")
speak(text="Nobody acts beyond that single cut until I relay the next sign.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👏 🖐]

## Thinking

The cut was right — the system confirms it, and the bomb has visibly changed state: display 1 → **4**, light green → **blue**, wire 5 now reads CUT. This is a multi-stage module. Blind's signs 👍 👏 🖐 read as "confirmed: cut wire 5" — the operator reporting the action done, as instructed.

Mute heard the system announcement but can't see the new values, so the critical thing is to broadcast the fresh state immediately so Mute can look up stage two. I relay the new readout in words, ask Mute for the next instruction in our sign code, and hold Blind still until it arrives.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Blind, confirmed and well done. The cut was correct. The bomb has changed: the display now shows the number 4. The light is now blue. Wire 5 shows as cut. Remaining wires, positions 1 to 7 left to right: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 cut, 6 purple, 7 blue. Keep your hands off the bomb until you hear my voice say cut wire and a number.")
speak(text="Mute: stage one succeeded. New state for the manual, stage two: display 4, light blue, seven positions with position 5 already cut, remaining wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue. Look up the next instruction and sign it to me in our code: OK sign, then clap, then the digit. If the module is now solved, sign both hands raised. If it needs something other than a cut, sign OK sign then describe it as best you can with the digits and yes or no signs, and I will work it through with you.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👏 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

## Thinking

Clean decode again: 👌 👏 🤟 = instruction, cut wire, digit 3 — **cut wire 3**, the yellow one in position 3. Blind is still holding as instructed. Same drill as stage one: relay the single cut, get the spoken report back, keep everyone frozen otherwise.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Relaying Mute's stage two instruction. Blind: cut wire 3. That is position 3 counting from the left, the wire I see as yellow. Cut only that one, then take your hands off and report aloud everything that changes: display, light, anything else.")
speak(text="Mute: instruction cut wire 3 relayed to Blind. Listen for the report. If solved, sign both hands raised. If another cut, sign OK sign then clap then digit. If wrong or dangerous, sign raised hand and I will shout for Blind to stop immediately.")
speak(text="Nobody does anything beyond that one cut until the next sign from Mute comes through me.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👏 🤟]

## Thinking

Stage two correct — display jumped to **7**, light now **purple**, position 3 cut. Three stages down possibly, but no completion signal yet. Same loop: broadcast the fresh state so Mute can consult the manual, and tell Mute explicitly that we may be near the end, since some manuals finish on a display value rather than another cut.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Blind, correct again. The bomb changed: the display now shows the number 7. The light is now purple. Wires 3 and 5 are cut. Remaining wires: 1 red, 2 white, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue. Hands off until you hear cut wire and a number from me.")
speak(text="Mute: stage two succeeded. New state for the manual: display 7, light purple, positions 3 and 5 cut, remaining wires 1 red, 2 white, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue. Look up stage three. If it is another cut, sign OK sign, clap, digit. If the module is solved or finishes without a cut, sign both hands raised. If it is done and needs no more action, I need to know that clearly, so use both hands raised for solved.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👏 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

## Thinking

Decode: 👌 👏 ☝ = instruction, cut wire, digit 1 — **cut wire 1**, the red wire at position 1. Blind is ready and holding. Relay the single cut, request the report, keep the protocol tight.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Relaying Mute's stage three instruction. Blind: cut wire 1. That is position 1, the far left wire, the one I see as red. Cut only that one, then hands off and report aloud everything that changes: display, light, sounds, anything.")
speak(text="Mute: instruction cut wire 1 relayed. Listen for the report. If solved, sign both hands raised. If another cut is needed, sign OK sign, clap, digit. If something is wrong, sign raised hand.")
speak(text="Same rule as before: nothing else gets touched until Mute's next sign reaches you through me.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👏 ☝]

## Thinking

Third correct cut — wire 1 gone, and this time the display held at 7 while the light changed purple → **green**. The system says the bomb changed, so this looks like another stage transition rather than completion, but only Mute's manual can say whether green-light-display-7 is "solved" or "stage four." Broadcast the full new state and ask for exactly that distinction.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Blind, correct again. The bomb changed: the display still shows the number 7, but the light has changed to green. Wires 1, 3 and 5 are cut. Remaining wires: 2 white, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue. Hands off until my next instruction.")
speak(text="Mute: stage three succeeded. New state for the manual: display 7, light green, positions 1, 3 and 5 cut, remaining wires 2 white, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue. Tell me clearly which of two things this is: if the module is now solved, sign both hands raised. If there is a stage four, sign OK sign, clap, digit for the next cut. If stage four needs something other than a cut, sign OK sign and then do your best with the digits and yes or no signs.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👏 🤘]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

## Thinking

Decode: 👌 👏 🤘 = instruction, cut wire, digit 7 — **cut wire 7**, the blue one at the far right. So not solved yet; there is a stage four. Blind is holding and ready. Same relay pattern, one cut, then report.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Relaying Mute's stage four instruction. Blind: cut wire 7. That is position 7, the far right wire, the one I see as blue. Cut only that one, then hands off and report aloud everything that changes: display, light, sounds, anything at all.")
speak(text="Mute: instruction cut wire 7 relayed. Listen for the report. If the module is solved, sign both hands raised. If another cut, sign OK sign, clap, digit. If wrong or dangerous, sign raised hand and I will call a stop.")
speak(text="Nobody touches anything beyond that single cut until the next sign comes through me.")
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👏 🤘]

## Thinking

Fourth correct cut — wire 7 gone, display changed 7 → **3**, light stayed green. Still no completion announcement, and four wires are now cut with three remaining (2 white, 4 orange, 6 purple). Relay the new state; Mute decides between "solved" and "stage five."

## Calls

```
speak(text="Blind, correct again. The bomb changed: the display now shows the number 3, the light stays green. Wires 1, 3, 5 and 7 are cut. Remaining wires: 2 white, 4 orange, 6 purple. Hands off until my next instruction.")
speak(text="Mute: stage four succeeded. New state for the manual: display 3, light green, positions 1, 3, 5 and 7 cut, remaining wires 2 white, 4 orange, 6 purple. Which is it: solved, in which case sign both hands raised, or another stage? If it is another cut, sign OK sign, clap, digit. If stage five needs something other than a cut, sign OK sign then describe it as best you can.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👏 🖖]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

## Thinking

Decode: 👌 👏 🖖 = instruction, cut wire, digit 4 — **cut wire 4**, the orange one. That leaves white at 2 and purple at 6 after this. Blind is holding. Same relay, one cut, then report.

## Calls

```
speak(text="Relaying Mute's stage five instruction. Blind: cut wire 4. That is position 4, the middle of the three remaining wires, the one I see as orange. Cut only that one, then hands off and report aloud everything that changes: display, light, sounds, anything at all.")
speak(text="Mute: instruction cut wire 4 relayed. Listen for the report. If solved, sign both hands raised. If another cut, sign OK sign, clap, digit. If wrong or dangerous, sign raised hand and I will call a stop.")
speak(text="Same rule: nothing beyond that single cut until the next sign comes through me.")
```
